128	def select_in_fold(T, cells, tr, tag, min_skip_share=0.0):
129	    """The nested-CV choice inside one training fold: the eligible cell with the largest kept-vs-skipped diff on the training rows.
130	    min_skip_share > 0 is the post-hoc variant (declared after the primary runs): the cell must also skip at least that share."""
131	    floor_n = FLOOR_N[T.tf] * len(tr) / T.is_mask.sum()
132	    best = None; n_elig = 0
133	    for c in cells:
134	        thr = c.fit(T, tr)
135	        full = np.ones(T.n, dtype=bool); full[tr] = c.apply(T, tr, thr)
136	        m = H.metrics(T, full, tr, tag, controls=False)
137	        if m["diff"] is None or m["kept_share"] < FLOOR_SHARE or m["kept_n"] < floor_n or (1 - m["kept_share"]) < min_skip_share: continue
138	        n_elig += 1
139	        if best is None or m["diff"] > best["diff"]:
140	            best = dict(diff=m["diff"], cell=c, thr=thr, kept_share=m["kept_share"], kept_n=m["kept_n"], control=None)

18	    {5,15,30}: category agree (k - j <= M and hv_dir == dir), disagree (k - j <= M and hv_dir opposite), none (no such bar

20	  gate cells (family h3/gate; 3 x 2 x 3 x 3 = 54 cells, each a ledger row): skip_if_disagree, skip_if_none, take_only_agree

49	def bar_frame(tf, folder):

52	    med = {N: g.transform(lambda s, N=N: s.shift(1).rolling(N, min_periods=5).median()).to_numpy() for N in NS}
53	    usable = ~b.fm_na.to_numpy()

59	    b["dir_num"] = np.sign(b.close.to_numpy() - b.open.to_numpy()).astype(int)

1	"""H4 "levels respected or broken" (BRIEF H4) through the harness. IS only; L1 primary, L0 robustness.
2	
3	    python h4_levels.py [--tf minute|5minute] [--labels L1,L0]
4	
5	Part A, the SETUP table (the build's as-of touch_* columns, data/README.md): touch episodes of the protected level / the nearest
6	  room edge / the nearest confirmed swing in the hour before k (a bar touches when low <= L <= high; consecutive touching bars
7	  are one episode); the last episode's verdict within 15 minutes after it, never past k: broke (a close beyond by > 0.5 x atr14
8	  on the far side), held, pending (window still open at k), none (no touch), na (no level).
9	  Descriptive: Foundation outcome by touch_<level>_last and by touch_<level>_n (0,1,2,3+). Gate cells (family h4/touch_gate, 9
10	  cells): skip when touch_<level>_last == broke / held / pending, level in {prot, room, swing}; nested CV over the 9; CPCV.
11	Part B, the episode study (IS bars only; labels of the level, not features): every touch episode of
12	  - a protected level: a maximal run of bars with the same engine `prot` value (bars.prot, as of the bar),
13	  - a room edge: lo and hi of every ST7/ST8 room over birth_bar <= i < retired_bar (fz_zones; retired_bar used only as the life end),
14	  - a confirmed swing: swings.price from conf_bar until the first close beyond it by > 0.5 x atr14 or the end of its session,
15	  with the same touch / episode / side / verdict rule as the build (verdict window 15 bars on 1 min, 3 bars on 5 min = 15 minutes,
16	  inside the touch bar's session; a window cut by the session end is `session_end`). side = sign(close before the episode - L)
17	  (open of the first touch bar when equal); break = a close on the far side by > 0.5 x atr14[last touch bar] inside the window.
18	  Aftermath from the verdict bar v (the breaking close for broke, the window end for held): move_n = sg x (close[v+n] - close[v]) /
19	  atr14[v] for n in {15, 30, 60} bars, sg = the break direction (broke) or the bounce direction away from the level (held);
20	  mfe_n = the best excursion in that direction; beyond_n = sg x (close[v+n] - L) / atr14[v] (the distance past the level, broke only);
21	  all inside v's session. Baseline: |close[i+n] - close[i]| / atr14[i] over every IS bar with the window inside its session.
22	  Retests: episodes of one level instance are numbered; prior_held = held episodes of the instance before this one; after_break =
23	  a broke episode of the instance came before. P(broke | prior_held) uses broke + held verdicts of episodes not after a break.
24	"""

52	def episodes(tp, L, a, b, kind, inst):
53	    """All touch episodes of level L over bars a..b (inclusive) with verdicts and aftermath."""
54	    lo, hi = tp.Ll[a:b + 1], tp.Hh[a:b + 1]
55	    hit = (lo <= L) & (hi >= L)
56	    if not hit.any(): return []
57	    idx = np.flatnonzero(hit) + a
58	    brk = np.diff(idx) > 1
59	    starts, ends = idx[np.r_[True, brk]], idx[np.r_[brk, True]]
60	    out = []; prior_held = 0; after_break = False
61	    for n_ep, (js, je) in enumerate(zip(starts, ends), start=1):
62	        ref = tp.Cc[js - 1] if js >= 1 else tp.O[js]
63	        side = np.sign(ref - L) or np.sign(tp.O[js] - L)
64	        rec = dict(kind=kind, inst=inst, level=float(L), js=int(js), je=int(je), touch_bars=int(je - js + 1), side=int(side), ep_index=n_ep,
65	                   prior_held=prior_held, after_break=after_break, session=int(tp.sess[js]), hhmm=tp.hhmm[js], verdict="na", v=None)
66	        if side == 0:
67	            out.append(rec); continue
68	        a_ = tp.A[je]; w0, w1 = je + 1, min(je + tp.W, tp.last[je])
69	        v = None
70	        if w1 >= w0:
71	            cc = tp.Cc[w0:w1 + 1]
72	            beyond = (L - cc) > BREAK_ATR * a_ if side > 0 else (cc - L) > BREAK_ATR * a_
73	            if beyond.any(): rec["verdict"] = "broke"; v = w0 + int(np.argmax(beyond))
74	            elif je + tp.W > tp.last[je]: rec["verdict"] = "session_end"
75	            else: rec["verdict"] = "held"; v = je + tp.W
76	        else: rec["verdict"] = "session_end"
77	        if v is not None:
78	            rec["v"] = int(v); sg = -side if rec["verdict"] == "broke" else side
79	            av = tp.A[v]
80	            for n in NS:
81	                if v + n <= tp.last[v] and av > 0:
82	                    rec[f"move_{n}"] = round(float(sg * (tp.Cc[v + n] - tp.Cc[v]) / av), 4)
83	                    ex = tp.Hh[v + 1:v + n + 1] if sg > 0 else tp.Ll[v + 1:v + n + 1]
84	                    rec[f"mfe_{n}"] = round(float(sg * (ex.max() if sg > 0 else ex.min()) - sg * tp.Cc[v]) / av, 4)
85	                    rec[f"beyond_{n}"] = round(float(sg * (tp.Cc[v + n] - L) / av), 4) if rec["verdict"] == "broke" else None
86	                else:
87	                    rec[f"move_{n}"] = rec[f"mfe_{n}"] = rec[f"beyond_{n}"] = None
88	        if rec["verdict"] == "held": prior_held += 1
89	        out.append(rec)
90	        if rec["verdict"] == "broke": after_break = True
91	    return out

94	def level_instances(tp):
95	    """(kind, inst, L, a, b) for every level instance alive inside the IS bars."""
96	    inst = []
97	    p = tp.prot; ok = ~np.isnan(p)
98	    change = np.r_[True, (p[1:] != p[:-1]) | (ok[1:] != ok[:-1])]
99	    starts = np.flatnonzero(change); ends = np.r_[starts[1:] - 1, len(p) - 1]
100	    for k_, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(starts, ends)):
101	        if ok[a]: inst.append(("prot", f"prot{k_}", float(p[a]), int(a), int(b)))
102	    z = tp.zones[tp.zones.birth_bar < tp.n_is]
103	    for r in z.itertuples():
104	        b = int(min((r.retired_bar - 1) if pd.notna(r.retired_bar) else tp.n_is - 1, tp.n_is - 1))
105	        if b >= r.birth_bar:
106	            inst.append(("room", f"{r.id}|lo", float(r.lo), int(r.birth_bar), b)); inst.append(("room", f"{r.id}|hi", float(r.hi), int(r.birth_bar), b))
107	    s = tp.swings[tp.swings.conf_bar < tp.n_is]
108	    for r in s.itertuples():

110	        seg = tp.Cc[a:end + 1]; at = tp.A[a:end + 1]
111	        beyond = (seg > L + BREAK_ATR * at) if r.kind == "H" else (seg < L - BREAK_ATR * at)
112	        b = a + int(np.argmax(beyond)) if beyond.any() else end
113	        inst.append(("swing", f"sw{r.seq}{r.kind}", L, a, b))
114	    return inst

1	"""POST-HOC (declared after the primary runs were read): the nested-CV selection with a minimum skipped share.
2	
3	The pre-registered selection (largest training-fold kept-vs-skipped diff subject to the harness KEPT floors) picked, on every
4	table, a cell that skips a handful of rows (2 of 826 on 5 min H2; 3 of 826 on 5 min H4 in the CPCV paths): a kept floor alone
5	does not bound the skipped set, and a two-row skip set has an unbounded diff. This variant adds `skipped share >= 0.10` to the
6	eligibility inside each training fold (nothing else changes: same cells, same folds, same criterion) and is counted in the family
7	as one more nested-CV trial (family '<study>/nested_cv_minskip' + its 11 CPCV paths). Both variants are reported; neither is
8	chosen on the pooled OOF.
9	
10	    python posthoc_minskip.py
11	"""
12	import os, sys, json, time, itertools
13	sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
14	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
15	sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]]
16	import numpy as np, pandas as pd
17	import h234_common as C
18	import harness as H
19	import h2_regime as H2, h3_volume as H3, h4_levels as H4
20	
21	MIN_SKIP = 0.10
22	log = C.Log(os.path.join(HERE, "posthoc_minskip.log"))
23	T0 = time.time()
24	
25	
26	def h3_cells(T, tf):
27	    feats = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(HERE, f"h3_{tf}_setup_hv_features.parquet"))
28	    f = feats.set_index("setup_i").loc[T.F.setup_i.to_numpy()].reset_index()
29	    sg = np.where(T.F.dir.astype(str).to_numpy() == "up", 1, -1)
30	    cats = {(v, N, M): H3.category(f, v, N, M, sg) for v, N, M in itertools.product(H3.VS, H3.NS, H3.MS)}
31	    return H3.cells_h3(cats)
32	
33	
34	if __name__ == "__main__":
35	    log(f"posthoc_minskip start {time.ctime()} ledger sha {H.ledger_sha()} min_skip_share {MIN_SKIP}")
36	    S = {}
37	    for tf in ("minute", "5minute"):
38	        for label in ("L1", "L0"):
39	            T = H.load(tf, label); tag = f"{tf}_{label}"
40	            for study, cells in (("h2", H2.cells_h2()), ("h3", h3_cells(T, tf)), ("h4", H4.cells_h4())):
41	                log(f"== {study} {tag}")
42	                res, chosen, dist, prow, cp_chosen = C.nested_cv(T, cells, study, __file__, log, min_skip_share=MIN_SKIP, suffix="_minskip")
43	                fam = C.family_stats(T, study, res, dist, tag + "_minskip")
44	                log(f"  family (incl. this row): {fam['candidates']} candidates, PBO diff {fam['pbo_diff']['pbo']}, SPA p {fam['spa']['spa_p']}, boot {fam['bootstrap_nested']['diff_ci']}, DSR p {fam['dsr_nested'].get('p')}, go {fam['go_no_go_nested']['passed']}")

46	                S[f"{study}/{tag}"] = dict(nested={k: res.get(k) for k in C.GRID_COLS if k != "cell"} | dict(chosen_per_block=chosen), cpcv=dist, cpcv_chosen=cp_chosen, family=fam)

44	## Designers' rationales
45	
46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
47	
48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
49	
50	Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.
51	
52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.
53	
54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.

62	### deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses (priority 1)
63	
64	**technique.** LLM-as-hypothesis-generator with pre-registration and a family-wise permutation test: Claude reads IS-only summaries of the per-SETUP feature table and writes a fixed, hashed list of candidate skip rules before any rule is scored.
65	
66	**what_it_answers.** Does a small set of human-readable rules, written from the user's own observations (sideways after repeated CHoCH, reaction to visibly high volume, respected vs broken levels, time of day, room read) plus what the IS marginals show, skip losers without skipping winners; and is the effect real after correcting for having proposed several rules at once? This is the only study whose raw output is already in ST13/ST14 config form.
67	
68	**method.** Inputs: fz_v3/<tf>/features.csv (IS rows only), the README feature dictionary, and the H1-H4 findings when available. Step 1, summaries the generator may see (script deep_llm_summaries.py): per as-of feature, decile table of Foundation mean net, win rate and count on IS; two-way tables for read x hour, n_choch_since_bos x dir, hv3_dir_agree x hv3_bars_since bucket, fz_visit_n x fz_read; nothing from OOS, no raw rows. Step 2, proposal: Claude writes deep_llm_rules_round1.json with <= 8 rules, each a conjunction of <= 3 comparisons on named features (e.g. {n_choch_since_bos >= 2, bars_since_bos > 36, range36_atr < 1.5} -> skip), with the reason in the user's words; the file's sha256 and timestamp are logged (deep_llm_register.txt) before step 3 runs. Step 3, scoring (deep_llm_eval.py): each rule on 5-fold purged session-blocked IS CV: kept n, skipped n, mean net kept vs skipped, permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p with 2,000 draws), losers-recall / precision, share of top-decile winners skipped, and the session-matched control percentile of the kept set; then a max-T permutation across all rules in the round (the family-wise p for the best rule), and Holm-adjusted single p's. Step 4: rules with Holm p < 0.05 and control percentile >= 95 on CV are combined greedily (order by CV kept-vs-skipped gain, stop when the marginal rule's gain < 200 INR/trade or when winners skipped rises) into a rule list of <= 8; a second round is allowed only if it is registered as round 2 and the multiplicity count carries over. Step 5: the frozen list scored once on OOS with the same table. Outputs: the round files, the CV table per rule, the OOS table, and the candidate ST13/ST14 gate block; a null result is reported as such.
69	
70	**leakage_controls.** Generator sees IS aggregates only, never OOS and never row-level forward returns; the proposal file is hashed before scoring so no rule is edited after seeing its number; features are the build's as-of columns only (fzpost_*, fwd_*, fnd_* excluded by column-name allow-list enforced in code); CV is purged/embargoed session-blocked; multiplicity is counted over every rule ever proposed across rounds and reported as a max-T permutation p; OOS run once, logged.
71	
72	**compute.** Under 5 CPU-minutes per timeframe (pandas tables and 2,000-draw permutations for <= 16 rules); peak memory under 300 MB. The real cost is Claude tokens for reading the summaries (~30k per timeframe).
73	
74	**libraries.** pandas, numpy; fz_report.permutation_p and fz_report.random_control imported read-only from the repo for the exact control definitions.
75	
76	**output_as_config.** Directly the ST13/ST14 gate block: {"gate": {"minute": {"rules": [{"if": [["n_choch_since_bos", ">=", 2], ["bars_since_bos", ">", 36]], "then": "skip", "source": "learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script deep_llm_eval.py, sha <..>, round 1 rule 3", "statistic": "CV kept-vs-skipped +A INR/trade, Holm p, control pct"}]}}}; each feature named must be one the fz/lab code can compute as-of at the SETUP bar, and the list is <= 8 rules of depth <= 3 as the brief requires.
77	
78	**novelty.** LLMs as zero-shot hypothesis proposers over tabular science data (Qi et al. 2023; Zhou et al. 2024 'Hypothesis generation with large language models'; FunSearch, Romera-Paredes et al. Nature 2024, for LLM-proposed heuristics scored by a fixed evaluator), disciplined by pre-registration (Nosek et al. 2018) against the garden of forking paths (Gelman & Loken 2013) and by the finance-native family-wise tests for data-snooped trading rules (White 2000 Reality Check; Hansen 2005 SPA; Westfall & Young max-T).
79	
80	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 3 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Trap: the generator writes rules after reading decile and two-way tables of IS mean net by feature, so the real family is every table cell it saw, not the <= 8 rules it wrote, and the 5-fold CV table is decoration for thresholds chosen on all of IS (garden of forking paths moved into the prompt). Fix: round 0 = rules from the user's words and the README feature dictionary only, hashed before any table is shown (this is H2-H4 in config form and the deliverable even if round 1 looks better); round 1 = tables built on IS blocks 1-6 only, scored on blocks 7-12 and vice versa (cross-fitted), with the number of table cells shown logged as the family size for max-T; both rounds through the harness ledger; features restricted to study 3's shortlist.

Fix: round 0 is blind (rules written from the user's words and the feature dictionary only, hashed before any labelled table exists); round 1 may see labelled tables, and its trials count in the ledger/PBO is the number of table cells shown (~1,000+), not 8. Use the harness splitter (12 blocks, 3-session embargo) instead of a private 5-fold. Every gate candidate goes through score(); kept-vs-skipped expectancy, session-matched random control (fz_report.random_control), permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p), CPCV 11 paths, go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV p5 diff > 0, DSR p < 0.1, kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300/80, top-1%-removed value > 0, slippage 8 pts survival). content.activeForm: Running the learned-gate family and modern-ML studies

content.subject: Walk-forward learn-after-each-trade policy with the trade journal (IS learning curve, continued through OOS); compose with rl.py for exit/size
content.description: fz_learn.py prototype: journal rows per SETUP (features, decision, reason, model state id, fill, exit, MFE/MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R, running equity/DD/PF); online learners (LinUCB/Thompson on logistic or tree-embedded model, online GBM refits, k-trade cadence); fractional Kelly sizing with max lots and daily loss stop; learning curve vs take-all and random control; deterministic replay.

content.subject: OOS opened once by one script for at most three frozen candidates (rule list, learner, ST7/ST8 comparator)

187	## 3. Selection note (why a post-hoc variant exists)
188	
189	The pre-registered nested-CV criterion (largest training-fold kept-vs-skipped diff subject to the harness *kept* floors) has no floor on the skipped set. On every table it selected a cell that skips a handful of rows (see the `chosen per training fold` tables: e.g. 5 min H2 skips 2 of 826 rows, 5 min H4 skips 3 in most CPCV training sets), because a two-row skip set has an unbounded diff. The harness go/no-go is what catches this (sign blocks, control percentile, PBO, DSR, the CPCV 5th percentile). `posthoc_minskip.py` re-runs the identical selection with `skipped share >= 10 %` added to the fold eligibility, declared after the primary rows were read and counted as one more trial per family (its rows are in the family PBO / SPA above). Nothing was chosen on the pooled OOF in either variant.
190	
191	## 4. What would falsify these findings
192	
193	- H2: a `h2/choch` or `h2/range` ledger row with diff > 0, control percentile >= 95, sign blocks >= 8 and a CPCV 5th-percentile diff > 0 under the nested-CV selection; or the bucket `n_choch_since_bos >= 2` showing a mean net below the other buckets by more than two standard errors on both timeframes and both labels.
194	- H3: a `h3/gate` row skipping >= 10 % of the SETUPs with diff > 0 at control percentile >= 95 in the nested-CV paths; or a bar aftermath table where the 30-bar move in the high-volume bar's direction differs from the baseline by more than 0.5 ATR.
195	- H4: a `h4/touch_gate` row with control percentile >= 95, sign blocks >= 8 and a positive CPCV 5th percentile; or an episode table where the absolute 30 / 60-bar move after a confirmed break exceeds the baseline by more than 0.5 ATR, or P(broke given prior_held >= 2) is lower than P(broke given prior_held = 0) by more than 0.2 on both timeframes with a positive Foundation expectancy at respected levels.
196	- Any of the above on a rebuild with a different `features.parquet` (the SETUP counts and the frozen kept set are pinned by `data/<tf>/meta.json`).
197	
198	## 5. Caveats
199	
200	- Bucket tables and the episode / bar-aftermath tables are descriptive decompositions (means, counts, iid standard errors, block sign counts). No p-value is attached to them; every question that needs one is a ledger row, and the kept-vs-skipped statistics of the 201 + 54 + 9 cells (plus the nested-CV rows) are the only kept-vs-skipped numbers in this study.
201	- The session-matched control percentile and the pooled diff disagree in sign on many cells (e.g. the 5 min `range_3h` cells: negative diff, control percentile 100). The control matches per-session kept counts, the diff pools all rows; a gate that skips whole sessions of the 5 min book (median two SETUPs per session) is matched trivially there. Both are reported; neither alone is the criterion.
202	- Under the harness `score`, a cell with a learned quantile is one ledger row on its OOF mask; its 12 fold thresholds differ by a few hundredths of an ATR (recorded in the grid CSV).
203	- L0 (the engine's uncut trade) is a robustness label only; on 1 min it runs to 70 sessions and its purge is coarser.
204	- The episode study's `prot` level instances are short on both timeframes (the engine moves the protected level at each swing update), so a protected level almost never sees a second episode: its retest counts are structural zeros, not evidence.
205	- The 1 min swing instances end at the first break or at their session's end by definition, so P(broke given prior_held = 0) on 1 min counts the many swings that break on their first touch shortly after confirmation.
206	- The recomputed volume baselines equal the build's `vol_med20_prior` / `vol_ratio20` / `vol_ratio60` exactly; the new per-SETUP H3 features equal the build's `hv2_*` / `hv3_*` (N = 20) and are identical on the truncated build for every SETUP before the cut (`trunc_20250630_120000`); the H4 episode features are labels of the level, never features.
207	- The ledger was appended by up to four processes in parallel (one per study x timeframe); the integrity counts are in the header (every line parses, every id has its vector file).
208	- On 5 min the `range_*_atr` terciles and quantiles use 12 / 36-bar windows; hour-of-day effects and the range rule are entangled (a session's range grows through the day).

# Extended as-of features (`fz_v3/out/features_ext/<tf>/ext_features.parquet`)

Built by `studies/ext_features/build_ext.py` (kernels in `ext_lib.py`), verified by `finalize.py` on the truncated tape, documented by `write_docs.py`.
One row per Foundation SETUP of `data/<tf>/features.parquet`, keyed by `setup_i` (join on it; the label and the split come from the base table through `harness.load`).
These columns are candidate features for the importance study (DESIGN_PANEL: quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, both judges) and nowhere else: no gate was searched here, no label was read.

Rows: minute 5326 SETUPs (5266 L1 units), 5minute 1012 SETUPs (1002 L1 units). Columns: 61 per timeframe (identical names on both).

## Conventions

- **as-of**: every value at SETUP bar `k` is a function of bars `<= k` (the SETUP bar included) and, for the fitted families, of a model frozen on the fit window.
- **fit window** = the IS bars of sessions 2021-10-01 .. 2023-09-30, the first IS half (489 sessions; 182,557 bars on 1m, 36,514 on 5m). Every z-scoring statistic, mixture, HMM, jump-model centroid and lambda, BOCPD standardisation and the FFD d* is estimated there and nowhere else: unsupervised, label-free; the second IS half and OOS never enter a fit. Inference is a forward pass over the whole tape from bar 0 with the frozen model. For bars inside the fit window the frozen statistics are, by construction, in-sample (a label-free in-sample effect, stated here; the truncation check below cannot see it because the cut is after the fit window).
- **gap-free log return**: `log(close_t / close_{t-1})`, except at a session's first bar where it is `log(close_t / open_t)`, so the overnight gap never enters a return-based statistic (the base README's window convention). FFD and BSADF work on the log close level itself and therefore see the gap as a level step (causal, stated).
- **same-session window**: cut at the session's first bar `s0 = k - session_bar`.
- **state relabelling**: for every GMM / HMM / jump model the states are ordered by ascending mean `(high-low)/atr14` so that state 0 is the quietest; the tables below give the means in original units.
- **truncation check**: the same builder ran on `data/<tf>/trunc_20250630_120000/` (bars up to 2025-06-30 12:00, same fit window) and every column was compared for every SETUP before the cut at tolerance 1e-9 (NaN pattern included); a differing column is dropped. Result below.

## Columns

| column | definition | causal argument | fit-window statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ffd_close_dstar` | fixed-width fractionally differentiated log close at d* (weights w_0 = 1, w_j = -w_{j-1}(d-j+1)/j, cut at |w| < 1e-4; the window length is reported below) | x_k = sum_j w_j log close_{k-j}: bars <= k only; direct convolution so the value does not depend on the tape length | fit window: IS bars of sessions 2021-10-01..2023-09-30 chooses d* by ADF (constant + 2 lags, statsmodels adfuller, 5% MacKinnon): the smallest d on the 0.1..1.0 grid whose ADF statistic passes; the ADF over all IS bars is reported next to it |
| `ffd_close_dstar_z60` | ffd_close_dstar minus its 60-bar rolling mean, over the 60-bar rolling std (ddof 1), bars k-59..k | rolling window ends at k | same d* |
| `ffd_vol_dstar` | the same FFD on log(max(volume, 1)) | as above | fit window: IS bars of sessions 2021-10-01..2023-09-30 chooses d* by the same ADF rule |
| `ffd_vol_dstar_z60` | 60-bar rolling z of ffd_vol_dstar | as above | same d* |
| `bsadf_close` | backward SADF (Phillips, Shi & Yu 2015): max over start bars s in [k-W+1, k-m+1] of the ADF t-statistic (constant, y_{t-1}, 2 lags of dy) of log close over bars s..k; W = 375 / 75 bars, m = 60 / 15 (1m / 5m); the window is demeaned by its first value (the intercept absorbs it) | every regression uses bars s..k <= k; the backward window may cross the previous session (bars, not time) | no fit: a deterministic function of bars <= k |
| `bsadf_close_win` | the window length (bars) at which bsadf_close attains its maximum | as above | no fit: a deterministic function of bars <= k |
| `cusum_events_60` | symmetric CUSUM filter (AFML 2.5.2.1) on gap-free log returns with the per-bar threshold h_t = atr14_t / close_t (S+ = max(0, S+ + r), S- = min(0, S- + r); an event when S+ > h or S- < -h, then both reset): events in bars (k-60, k] | the filter runs forward over the tape; the count reads events at bars <= k | no fit: a deterministic function of bars <= k |

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
for tf, W in (("5minute",3),("minute",15)):
    E = pd.read_parquet(f"studies/h2_h3_h4/h4_{tf}_episodes.parquet")
    b = pd.read_parquet(f"data/{tf}/bars.parquet", columns=["i","session_idx"])
    last = b.groupby("session_idx")["i"].transform("max").to_numpy()
    cut = (E.je.to_numpy() + W) > last[E.je.to_numpy()]
    print(tf, "episodes", len(E), "| window cut by session end:", int(cut.sum()), "| of which verdict broke:", int((cut & (E.verdict=="broke")).sum()), "held:", int((cut & (E.verdict=="held")).sum()), "session_end:", int((cut & (E.verdict=="session_end")).sum()))
    print("   verdict counts:", E.verdict.value_counts().to_dict())
    # P(broke) table sanity vs FINDINGS for 5min prot prior_held 0
    D = E[E.verdict.isin(["broke","held"]) & ~E.after_break]
    g = D[D.kind=="room"].groupby(np.where(D[D.kind=="room"].prior_held>=3,"3+",D[D.kind=="room"].prior_held.astype(str))).verdict.apply(lambda s: (len(s), round((s=="broke").mean(),4)))
    print("   room p_broke by prior_held:", g.to_dict())
EOF

content.description: fz_learn.py prototype: journal rows per SETUP (features, decision, reason, model state id, fill, exit, MFE/MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R, running equity/DD/PF); online learners (LinUCB/Thompson on logistic or tree-embedded model, online GBM refits, k-trade cadence); fractional Kelly sizing with max lots and daily loss stop; learning curve vs take-all and random control; deterministic replay.

content.subject: OOS opened once by one script for at most three frozen candidates (rule list, learner, ST7/ST8 comparator)
content.description: fz_v3/out/oos_once.py reads frozen candidate JSON + sha; scores OOS 2026-01-01..2026-09-25 with random control, permutation p, kept-vs-skipped, winner recall; the learner continues updating through OOS as it would live. Caveats: OOS window = published lab window, used by ST9-12 exit grid.

content.subject: Report survivors and plan to the user before creating strategy files; then code ST13/ST14 (fz_learn.py, strategy_13/14.json, tests, docs, S49, REPORT.md)
content.description: Tell the user the plan and survivors first. Then: fz_learn.py beside fz.py (entry_rule fz_v3), strategy_13.json / strategy_14.json with every threshold / weight / hyper-parameter as a sourced key, journal as an output table, deterministic replay, engine.py untouched, ST5-ST8 bit-for-bit unchanged; extend tests/test_fz_parity.py and tests/test_truncation.py; FZ.md, README.md, S49 (Rule 0), fz_v3/out/REPORT.md, QUALITY.md.

content.subject: Commit and push on research/strategy-lab-pwxiug (code, strategy files, tests, docs, fz_v3/out only); open draft PR
content.description: Never commit results/, cache/, web/. Push with -u; create a draft PR if none exists.

content.subject: rocket_ceiling: benchmark, write rocket_ceiling.py, run under nohup, write FINDINGS.md + findings.json
content.description: Study rocket_ceiling under OUT/studies/rocket_ceiling: window tensor (L=60, 7 channels), 2,000 MiniRocket-style kernels, fold-fitted biases, L2 logistic probe with nested GroupKFold alpha, comparators (tabular HGB, PCA-16 window probe, stacked HGB), 12 purged splits + 66 CPCV splits -> 11 paths, AUC gain distribution, pre-registered stop at CPCV p5 gain < 0.03, gates at skip 30/50/70% as ledger rows (rocket/<model>), truncation check of the window tensor, timing + RSS, FINDINGS.md and findings.json.
